title: Enrich the claims with visits and providers
prompt:
Finance wants each claim next to what happened at the visit and who treated the patient. The visits are in `encounters`, nested: `vitals` is a struct and `diagnosis_codes` an array. The feed also changed on 1 January 2026, when `discharge_disposition` was added: older visits have nothing there.

Write `silver_encounters(encounters)`, one flat row per visit, then `enriched_claims(claims, encounters, providers)`: each silver claim with its visit and its provider's specialty.
rules: `temperature_c` comes from `vitals`. A value above 45 was sent in Fahrenheit: convert it, (F − 32) × 5 / 9, rounded to 1 decimal.
`discharge_disposition` is `not_collected` for visits that started before 2026-01-01, `not_applicable` when a later visit has none, and the value otherwise.

`enriched_claims` keeps every silver claim, even one whose visit is missing. A claim with no `provider_id` takes the visit's; `specialty` comes from `providers` for the provider the claim ends up with.
hints: `F.col("vitals.temperature_c")` reads a struct field, and `F.col("diagnosis_codes")[0]` the first array element. Both are missing when the struct or array is.
Left-join the visits on `encounter_id`, fill the provider with `F.coalesce("provider_id", "visit_provider_id")`, and only then left-join `providers.select("provider_id", "specialty")`.
explanation: Silver flattens nested data once, so no reader has to know the feed's shape: struct fields become columns with `vitals.temperature_c`, and the first diagnosis comes out of the array with `[0]`. Normalising here fixes the three Fahrenheit readings for everyone. The new column needs care: before 1 January 2026 it didn't exist, so a missing value means 'not collected', not 'not applicable'. Checking the date first keeps the two meanings apart. In the enrichment, left joins keep every claim even when a lookup fails, so no money disappears. The order of the two joins matters: the claim's missing provider has to be filled from the visit before looking up the specialty, or those claims would get none.
